step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows Sisense's analytics solution deployed on AWS. User traffic originates from mobile devices or a dashboard interface and flows through an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) into an Amazon EKS cluster running compute pods on EC2 instances. Data is ingested from multiple sources, including on-premises databases, source Redshift clusters, RDS, and S3 buckets (accessed via Athena and cataloged by Glue). Processed 'hot' data is written to an FSx for Lustre shared file system for fast in-memory access and backed up to an S3 bucket for disaster recovery. 'Warm' terabyte-scale data is stored and queried directly in an Amazon Redshift data warehouse.

graph.name: Sisense Analytics Architecture on AWS
graph.notes: Sisense's hybrid big data analytics architecture ingests data from disparate sources into EKS containerized workloads, utilizing FSx for Lustre for fast hot-data processing backed by S3, and Redshift for large-scale warm data querying.
